Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ's):
1. What is the Metropolis TruHealth Active Male package?
The Metropolis TruHealth Active Male is a preventive health checkup designed for Indian men aged 25 to 55, especially those with a family history of illness or a lifestyle-linked risk profile. It covers 70+ parameters in a single blood and urine sample, including male-specific markers like total testosterone and Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA), along with full panels for heart, liver, kidney, thyroid, diabetes, complete blood count, vitamins and cancer-screening markers. The package is processed at Metropolis Healthcares NABL-accredited laboratory and is bookable online through bookmytest.co.in.
2. What tests are included in the Metropolis TruHealth Active Male package?
The TruHealth Active Male package by Metropolis includes Complete Blood Count (CBC), Lipid Profile, Liver Function Test (LFT), Kidney Function Test (KFT), Thyroid Profile (T3, T4, TSH), HbA1c and Fasting Blood Sugar, Vitamin D 25-Hydroxy, Vitamin B12, Iron Studies, Total Testosterone, Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA), HsCRP for cardiac inflammation, and a complete Urine Routine examination. The exact parameter list, normal ranges and a sample Metropolis report are visible on the package page on bookmytest.co.in before booking.
3. Why is testosterone testing important for Indian men?
Testosterone influences energy, muscle mass, fat distribution, libido, mood, sleep quality and bone density. Low testosterone in Indian men is increasingly being diagnosed even in the 30s, driven by obesity, sleep deprivation, chronic stress and metabolic syndrome. Symptoms include persistent fatigue, reduced gym performance, abdominal weight gain, loss of morning erections and irritability. The Metropolis TruHealth Active Male package includes a morning total testosterone test that confirms whether levels are below the normal adult male range of roughly 300 to 1,000 ng/dL.
4. What does the PSA test in this package detect?
PSA, or Prostate-Specific Antigen, is a protein produced by the prostate gland. Elevated levels can indicate benign prostate enlargement, prostatitis or, in some cases, prostate cancer. The normal range is generally below 4 ng/mL, though it varies with age. PSA screening through the Metropolis TruHealth Active Male package is particularly important for men above 45, men above 40 with a family history of prostate cancer, and those experiencing urinary symptoms such as frequent night-time urination, weak stream or incomplete bladder emptying.
5. Is fasting required for the Metropolis TruHealth Active Male test?
Yes, a 10 to 12 hour overnight fast is required. Fasting is essential for accurate lipid profile, fasting glucose, insulin and testosterone readings, all of which are affected by recent food intake or time of day. Plain water is allowed and recommended during the fasting window. Continue your prescription medication unless your doctor advises otherwise, and avoid alcohol for 24 hours and intense gym workouts for 12 hours before the Metropolis phlebotomist arrives for sample collection.
6. At what age should Indian men start taking the Metropolis full body checkup?
Indian men should begin annual preventive health checkups from age 25, especially with a desk job, irregular sleep, family history of diabetes, heart disease or thyroid disorder, or a BMI above 25. From age 40, PSA and cardiac risk markers become particularly important. The Metropolis TruHealth Active Male package is built around exactly this profile, combining metabolic, hormonal and male-specific screening in a single sample. Annual repeat testing helps build a personal baseline so any drift in HbA1c, LDL or testosterone is caught early.
7. Is Metropolis a trusted lab for full body checkups in India?
Yes. Metropolis Healthcare is one of Indias largest and most respected diagnostic chains, with NABL-accredited laboratories, decades of clinical reputation and a panel of senior pathologists. The TruHealth series of preventive packages is curated by Metropolis specialists and is widely used by corporate health programmes, insurance partners and individual customers across India. Booking the Metropolis TruHealth Active Male through bookmytest.co.in gives you the same lab quality with transparent partner pricing and free home sample collection.
8. How long does it take to receive the Metropolis TruHealth Active Male report?
Reports are delivered within 24 to hours of sample pickup. Samples collected in the early morning slot typically reach the Metropolis processing laboratory the same day, and digital reports are emailed and sent on WhatsApp by the next evening. A few specialised parameters like Vitamin B12 or hormonal markers may need an additional 12 hours. You can also download the report anytime from your bookmytest.co.in dashboard or directly from the Metropolis TruHealth portal using your registered mobile number.
9. Is home sample collection available across India for this Metropolis package?
Yes, free home sample collection by trained Metropolis phlebotomists is available across 2,000+ pincodes covering all major metro cities, tier-2 cities and most tier-3 towns in India. After booking on bookmytest.co.in, the phlebotomist arrives at your address in a 2-hour slot of your choosing, ideally between 6 AM and 10 AM for fasting samples. There are no hidden charges for the visit, report generation or digital delivery anywhere in India.
10. What should I do if my Metropolis TruHealth report shows borderline values?
Borderline values are early warnings rather than disease diagnoses, and most of them are reversible through lifestyle changes. A fasting glucose of 105 mg/dL, an HbA1c of 5.8%, an LDL of 110 mg/dL or a testosterone of 290 ng/dL are all borderline and respond well to weight reduction, strength training, improved sleep, reduced alcohol and targeted supplementation. Consult a physician, repeat the Metropolis test in three months, and track the trend rather than reacting to a single value.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ's):
1. What is the TruHealth Active Female package?
The TruHealth Active Female package is a preventive health checkup built specifically for Indian women aged 25 to 55. It covers 70 to 85 parameters in a single blood and urine sample, including female-relevant markers like thyroid profile, iron studies, Vitamin D, Vitamin B12 and hormonal indicators, along with standard panels for heart, liver, kidney, diabetes and complete blood count. It is designed to catch conditions like hypothyroidism, anaemia, PCOS-linked metabolic changes and Vitamin D deficiency in their early, reversible stage.
2. What tests are included in TruHealth Active Female?
The package includes Complete Blood Count, Lipid Profile, Liver Function Test, Kidney Function Test, Thyroid Profile (T3, T4, TSH), HbA1c and Fasting Blood Sugar, Vitamin D 25-Hydroxy, Vitamin B12, Iron Studies (Iron, Ferritin, TIBC), Calcium, HsCRP for cardiac inflammation, and a complete Urine Routine examination. The exact parameter list, normal ranges and sample report are visible on the package page on bookmytest.co.in before you confirm the booking.
3. Why is thyroid testing important for Indian women?
Hypothyroidism is significantly more common in Indian women than men, with prevalence rising sharply after the age of 30 and around pregnancy or menopause. It can silently cause fatigue, weight gain, hair fall, irregular periods, infertility, low mood and dry skin — symptoms often mistaken for everyday stress. A simple TSH, T3 and T4 blood test confirms the diagnosis. Untreated hypothyroidism affects cholesterol, fertility and heart health, which is why annual thyroid screening is strongly advised for adult women.
4. Why is iron deficiency screening important for women?
Iron-deficiency anaemia is one of the most under-diagnosed conditions in Indian women, affecting more than half of women of reproductive age. Heavy menstrual flow, pregnancy, breastfeeding and vegetarian diets all increase the risk. Symptoms include persistent tiredness, breathlessness on stairs, hair fall, brittle nails, pale skin and poor concentration. The Active Female package tests haemoglobin, ferritin, iron and TIBC together, which gives a far more accurate picture than haemoglobin alone.
5. Is fasting required for TruHealth Active Female?
Yes, a 10 to 12 hour overnight fast is required. Fasting is essential for accurate lipid profile, fasting glucose and insulin readings, all of which are affected by recent food intake. Plain water is allowed and recommended during the fasting window. Continue your regular prescription medication unless your doctor advises otherwise. Avoid alcohol for 24 hours and heavy exercise for 12 hours before the sample is drawn, as both can temporarily alter liver enzymes and other readings.
6. At what age should Indian women start taking a full body checkup?
Indian women should begin annual preventive health checkups from age 25, especially with sedentary jobs, irregular cycles, family history of thyroid disorder, diabetes or PCOS, or a BMI above 25. From age 35, additional markers like Vitamin D, calcium and bone-health indicators become particularly important. The TruHealth Active Female package is designed for exactly this profile, combining metabolic, hormonal and nutritional screening in a single blood draw.
7. Can I take the TruHealth Active Female test during my period?
You can, but a few parameters may be affected. Haemoglobin and ferritin can read slightly lower during menstruation, and inflammatory markers may be marginally elevated. For the most accurate results, ideally schedule the test for the week after your period ends. If your booking is urgent or your cycle is irregular, going ahead is still fine — just inform the phlebotomist so the result can be interpreted correctly by your physician.
8. How long does it take to receive the report?
Reports are delivered within 12 hours after sample reaches to lab. Samples collected in the early morning slot typically reach the central processing laboratory the same day, and digital reports are emailed and sent on WhatsApp by the next evening. A few specialised parameters like Vitamin B12 or thyroid hormones may need an additional 12 hours. You can also download the report anytime from your Metropolis dashboard using your registered mobile number.
9. Is home sample collection available across India for this package?
Yes, free home sample collection is available across 2,000+ pincodes covering all major metro cities, tier-2 cities and most tier-3 towns in India. After booking on bookmytest.co.in, a trained female phlebotomist (on request) arrives at your address in a 2-hour slot of your choosing, ideally between 6 AM and 10 AM for fasting samples. There are no hidden charges for the phlebotomist visit, report generation or digital delivery anywhere in India.
10. What should I do if my report shows borderline values?
Borderline values are early warnings rather than disease diagnoses, and most of them are reversible through lifestyle changes. A TSH of 4.8 mIU/L, a ferritin of 28 ng/mL, an HbA1c of 5.8% or a Vitamin D of 22 ng/mL are all borderline and respond well to balanced nutrition, iron-rich diet, sunlight exposure, sleep correction and targeted supplementation. Consult a physician, repeat the test in three months, and track the trend rather than reacting to a single value.

The Thyrocare TB Whole Genome Sequencing Package offers advanced molecular testing to identify the complete genetic profile of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacterium. By using cutting-edge genome sequencing technology, Thyrocare ensures high-precision detection and in-depth analysis to support timely and effective treatment planning for tuberculosis.
2. Who should opt for the Thyrocare TB Whole Genome Sequencing test?
This test is ideal for patients who have been diagnosed with tuberculosis and are not responding to standard treatment, those with suspected drug-resistant TB, individuals experiencing recurrent TB infections, or patients requiring a personalized antibiotic strategy. Thyrocares TB Whole Genome Sequencing is designed to help healthcare providers determine the most appropriate and effective medication based on the patient’s bacterial profile.
3. Is fasting or special preparation required for the Thyrocare TB Genome Sequencing test?
No fasting or special dietary preparations are needed for this test. The test requires a sputum sample, preferably collected from the first cough in the morning. Thyrocare’s home collection services ensure that the sample is collected in a safe and hygienic manner for further genomic analysis.

The TB Whole Genome Sequencing test by Thyrocare supports India’s mission to eliminate tuberculosis by providing early detection of drug resistance and enabling targeted therapy. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ's):
1. What is the Thyrocare Fat Soluble Vitamins Profile and what does it test?
The Thyrocare Fat Soluble Vitamins Profile is a focused blood test that measures the four fat-soluble vitamins essential for human health — Vitamin A (Retinol), Vitamin D (25-Hydroxy), Vitamin E (Tocopherol) and Vitamin K. These vitamins are absorbed and transported through dietary fat, and unlike water-soluble vitamins, they are stored long-term in body fat and liver tissue.
2. What is the difference between fat-soluble and water-soluble vitamins?
Vitamins fall into two groups based on how they dissolve and are stored. Water-soluble vitamins — the entire B-complex and Vitamin C — dissolve in water, are not stored by the body and must be replenished daily through food. Fat-soluble vitamins — A, D, E and K — dissolve in fat, are stored in the liver and adipose tissue, and last for weeks to months in the body. This storage capacity makes fat-soluble vitamins prone to two extremes — chronic deficiency despite a recent diet improvement, or accumulation to toxic levels with excessive supplementation. The Thyrocare Fat Soluble Vitamins Profile measures all four in one sample.
3. Why test fat-soluble vitamins separately instead of doing a full vitamin panel?
A focused fat-soluble vitamin test is the right choice when clinical concerns relate specifically to bone health (Vitamin D), vision and immunity (Vitamin A), antioxidant defense (Vitamin E), or blood clotting (Vitamin K) — without paying for the full B-complex panel. The Thyrocare Fat Soluble Vitamins Profile is more affordable than the Complete Vitamins Profile, making it the smart choice when your physician has specifically asked for ADEK evaluation, or when monitoring fat-soluble vitamin levels after supplementation or surgery. The Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile is the better fit when you have multi-system symptoms suggesting deficiencies across both vitamin groups.
4. Who specifically should take the Thyrocare Fat Soluble Vitamins Profile?
The Thyrocare Fat Soluble Vitamins Profile is particularly recommended for Indian adults with fat-malabsorption conditions like Crohns disease, ulcerative colitis, celiac disease, chronic pancreatitis or cystic fibrosis; people who have undergone bariatric (weight-loss) surgery; those on chronic low-fat diets or cholesterol-lowering medications like statins; individuals with liver or gallbladder disease; senior citizens with declining nutrient absorption; people with confirmed Vitamin D deficiency wanting to retest after supplementation; and adults with symptoms pointing to bone, vision, immunity or clotting issues.
5. Can fat-soluble vitamins cause toxicity if over-supplemented?
Yes, this is one of the most important reasons to test rather than guess. Unlike water-soluble vitamins which the body simply excretes when in excess, fat-soluble vitamins accumulate in the liver and adipose tissue. Excess Vitamin A can cause headache, liver damage, bone weakening and even birth defects in pregnancy. Excess Vitamin D can cause hypercalcaemia, kidney stones and kidney damage. Vitamin K excess is rare but can interfere with blood thinners. The Thyrocare Fat Soluble Vitamins Profile is therefore essential before and during high-dose supplementation, particularly with multivitamin formulas commonly self-prescribed in India.
6. What symptoms suggest fat-soluble vitamin deficiency?
Symptoms vary by vitamin. Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness, dry eyes, frequent infections and dry skin. Vitamin D deficiency causes bone and muscle pain, fatigue, low immunity and mood changes. Vitamin E deficiency causes muscle weakness, vision issues and impaired immunity. Vitamin K deficiency causes easy bruising, prolonged bleeding from minor cuts and bleeding gums. Many of these symptoms overlap with other conditions, which is why the Thyrocare Fat Soluble Vitamins Profile gives a definitive answer in one sample rather than testing each vitamin separately or guessing through trial-and-error supplementation.
7. Is fasting required for the Thyrocare Fat Soluble Vitamins Profile test?
A 10 to 12 hour overnight fast is generally recommended for the most accurate readings of all four fat-soluble vitamins. Because these vitamins are absorbed with dietary fat, recent meals can transiently raise circulating levels and obscure your true storage status. Plain water is allowed during fasting. Importantly, pause any vitamin or multivitamin supplements for 48 to 72 hours before the Thyrocare test if you want an honest baseline — otherwise the report reflects recent supplementation rather than your bodys actual stored vitamin reserves. Continue prescription medication unless your doctor advises otherwise.
8. How is the Thyrocare Fat Soluble Vitamins Profile different from a standalone Vitamin D test?
A standalone Vitamin D test measures only 25-Hydroxy Vitamin D. The Thyrocare Fat Soluble Vitamins Profile adds Vitamins A, E and K to give a complete picture of all four fat-soluble vitamins in one sample. This is particularly important because fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies tend to occur together — if you are Vitamin D deficient due to fat-malabsorption, low-fat diet or post-bariatric surgery, you are likely also low in A, E and K. Addressing only Vitamin D leaves three blind spots unchecked, which is why the Thyrocare ADEK panel is the more clinically complete option whenever multi-vitamin deficiency is suspected.
9. How does fat malabsorption or bariatric surgery affect fat-soluble vitamins?
Conditions that impair fat absorption — Crohns disease, ulcerative colitis, celiac disease, chronic pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis, gallbladder disease, liver disease and weight-loss (bariatric) surgery — directly disrupt the bodys ability to absorb Vitamins A, D, E and K from food. This makes fat-soluble vitamin deficiency extremely common in these patient populations, often even on a healthy diet, because the absorption mechanism itself is impaired. Most gastroenterologists and bariatric surgeons in India recommend an annual Thyrocare Fat Soluble Vitamins Profile to monitor and correct these deficiencies before complications develop.
10. How do I book the Thyrocare Fat Soluble Vitamins Profile with home collection in India?
Booking is a simple three-step process on bookmytest.co.in — select the Thyrocare Fat Soluble Vitamins Profile, enter your address and preferred 2-hour home collection slot (ideally between 6 AM and 10 AM for fasting), and confirm with online payment. A trained Thyrocare phlebotomist arrives at your home for sample collection, which takes around 5 minutes. The sample is sent to Thyrocares NABL-accredited central laboratory for processing, and digital reports are delivered to email and WhatsApp within 24 hours.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ's):
1. What is the Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile test?
The Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile is a comprehensive blood test that measures the levels of all essential vitamins required for human health in a single sample. It covers both fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) and water-soluble vitamins (B-complex group including B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B7, B9 and B12). The test is processed at Thyrocares NABL-accredited central laboratory in Mumbai, which is among Indias largest and most automated pathology facilities. Booking the Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile through bookmytest.co.in includes free pan-India home sample collection and digital reports within 24–48 hours.
2. What vitamins are included in the Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile?
The Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile typically includes Vitamin D (25-Hydroxy), Vitamin B12 (Cyanocobalamin), Vitamin B9 (Folate), Vitamin B1 (Thiamine), Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin), Vitamin B3 (Niacin), Vitamin B5 (Pantothenic Acid), Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxal Phosphate), Vitamin B7 (Biotin), Vitamin A (Retinol), Vitamin E (Tocopherol) and Vitamin K. Vitamin C may be included in extended variants. The exact parameter list is visible on the Thyrocare test page on bookmytest.co.in before booking, along with current pricing and a sample report format.
3. Why is vitamin testing especially important for Indian adults?
India has one of the highest rates of Vitamin D deficiency in the world — research indicates that more than 70% of Indian adults are deficient despite abundant sunshine, mainly due to indoor lifestyles, skin pigmentation, vegetarian diets and pollution. Vitamin B12 deficiency is similarly widespread, affecting nearly half of Indian vegetarians since B12 occurs primarily in animal-source foods. The Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile screens these and other deficiencies in one go, replacing what would otherwise be five to six separate tests at significantly higher combined cost.
4. What symptoms indicate I should take the Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile?
You should consider the Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile if you experience persistent unexplained fatigue, hair fall and dry skin, brittle nails, frequent muscle cramps, bone or joint pain, tingling or numbness in the hands and feet, recurrent mouth ulcers, low mood, brain fog and poor concentration, frequent infections, or slow wound healing. Any combination of these symptoms in an Indian adult often points to multiple overlapping vitamin deficiencies — which a single comprehensive panel like the Thyrocare profile can pinpoint far more efficiently than testing one vitamin at a time.
5. Is the Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile suitable for vegetarians and vegans?
Yes, and it is particularly valuable for Indian vegetarians and vegans, who are at significantly higher risk of multiple vitamin deficiencies. Vitamin B12 occurs almost exclusively in animal-source foods, so a vegetarian or vegan diet without fortified foods or supplementation almost always leads to deficiency over time. Vitamin D, B6 and certain B-complex vitamins are also commonly low in plant-only diets. The Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile is well-suited as an annual baseline test for Indian vegetarians and vegans, helping detect deficiencies before they cause clinical symptoms like anaemia or neurological issues.
6. Is fasting required for the Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile test?
A 10 to 12 hour overnight fast is generally recommended for the Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile, particularly because certain fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) and metabolic-context markers are more accurate after fasting. Plain water is allowed and recommended during the fasting window. Continue prescribed medication unless your doctor specifies otherwise. Importantly, vitamin and multivitamin supplements should ideally be paused for 24 hours before the test if you are looking for an honest baseline — otherwise the report will reflect recent supplementation rather than your bodys actual stored levels.
7. How often should I repeat the Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile?
Once a year for most healthy Indian adults as part of annual preventive screening. Every 3 to 6 months if you are actively supplementing to correct a confirmed deficiency — for example, after starting Vitamin D or B12 therapy on a doctors advice. Twice a year for strict vegetarians, vegans, senior citizens, women going through menopause, post-pregnancy mothers, and people recovering from chronic illness, surgery or long-term medication use. Tracking trends across multiple Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile reports gives a far clearer picture than any one-time test.
8. Can the Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile track supplementation effectiveness?
Yes, this is one of the most practical uses of the test. After your physician prescribes vitamin supplementation — most commonly Vitamin D, B12 or folate for confirmed deficiencies — repeating the Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile after 3 to 6 months shows whether the supplement dose is actually correcting the deficiency. Around 30% of Indian patients on standard vitamin supplements continue to read low even after months of therapy, often because of poor absorption, wrong supplement form, or inadequate dose. The repeat Thyrocare report catches this and lets your doctor adjust treatment.
9. Will the Thyrocare test accurately detect Vitamin D and B12 deficiency?
Yes. Vitamin D is measured as 25-Hydroxy Vitamin D, which is the global gold-standard marker for Vitamin D status, with established reference ranges (30–100 ng/mL is normal). Vitamin B12 is measured using a chemiluminescence immunoassay with a normal range of approximately 200–900 pg/mL. Thyrocares NABL-accredited laboratory uses fully automated analysers and follows internal and external quality control protocols that meet international pathology accuracy standards. The Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile is widely accepted by Indian physicians, endocrinologists and nutritionists for clinical decision-making.
10. How do I book the Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile with home collection in India?
Booking is a simple three-step process on bookmytest.co.in — select the Thyrocare Complete Vitamins Profile, enter your address and preferred 2-hour home collection slot and confirm with online payment. A trained Thyrocare phlebotomist arrives at your home for sample collection, which takes around 5 minutes. The sample is sent to Thyrocares NABL-accredited central laboratory for processing, and digital reports are delivered to email and WhatsApp within 24 hours.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ's):
Q. What tests are included in the Thyrocare Summer Wellness with Vitamins & Electrolytes Package?
Ans.
This specially curated summer health package by Thyrocare includes 107 parameters to evaluate essential vitamins, minerals, and electrolytes required for optimal hydration and energy during hot weather. The profile consists of Vitamin D, Vitamin B12, along with comprehensive health assessments such as Complete Blood Count (CBC), Liver Function Test (LFT), Kidney Function Test (KFT), Lipid Profile, Thyroid Profile, Diabetes markers. These tests are conducted using Thyrocare’s fully automated and NABL/ISO-certified diagnostic systems to ensure accurate and reliable results.
Q. Who should opt for the Thyrocare Summer Wellness with Vitamins & Electrolytes test?
Ans.
This package is ideal for individuals who experience symptoms related to dehydration, fatigue, low immunity, muscle cramps, or poor energy levels during the summer months. It is also suitable for those who are frequently exposed to high temperatures, have outdoor work schedules, or want to maintain optimal wellness during seasonal changes. The test helps assess deficiencies or imbalances that can worsen in summer and supports preventive care planning.
Q. Is fasting required before taking the Thyrocare Summer Wellness test?
Ans.
Yes, fasting is required before the sample collection. A fasting period of 8 to 12 hours is recommended to ensure accurate readings for metabolic and vitamin-related markers, especially blood sugar, lipid profile, and insulin levels. During fasting, only plain water is permitted.
Q. How is the sample collected for the Thyrocare Summer Wellness test?
Ans.
Thyrocare provides free home sample collection services across India. A certified phlebotomist will visit your location at the scheduled time to collect the required blood and urine samples. The collected samples are transported securely to Thyrocare’s advanced, automated diagnostic laboratories that are accredited by NABL and ISO, ensuring precision and reliability at every step.
Q. What is the cost of the Thyrocare Summer Wellness with Vitamins & Electrolytes Package?
Ans.
The Thyrocare Summer Wellness package is priced at Rs 1,949 for one individual. There is also a value pack available for two people at Rs 2,998 . The pricing includes all 107 tests, home sample collection, and delivery of digital reports via SMS and email, offering exceptional value for preventive health screening.
Q. When will I receive my test report from Thyrocare?
Ans.
Test results are typically delivered within 24 to 48 hours after sample collection. Thyrocare ensures quick turnaround with digital reports shared directly to your registered mobile number and email ID. This allows you to access and share your health report conveniently and securely.
Q. Why choose Thyrocare for this summer health checkup?
Ans.
Thyrocare is a leading name in diagnostic services with over 25 years of experience and a strong presence across India. It is known for offering affordable health packages, home collection services, and high-precision results using fully automated laboratory infrastructure. The Summer Wellness with Vitamins & Electrolytes Package is designed specifically for seasonal health challenges, helping individuals stay energized, hydrated, and nutritionally balanced through expert screening and timely insights.
Q. Does this package include electrolyte tests like Sodium, Potassium, and Chloride?
Ans.
Yes, the Summer Wellness Package includes key electrolyte markers such as Sodium, Potassium, Chloride, and Calcium, which are crucial for maintaining fluid balance, preventing dehydration, and ensuring optimal muscle and nerve function during the hot weather.
Q. Can children or elderly people take this test?
Ans.
Yes, this test is suitable for all age groups, especially elderly individuals and children who may be more vulnerable to heat-related imbalances. It’s advisable to consult a healthcare provider before booking for children below 12 years.
